title_en: Zhang Guiping v. Wang Hua — dispute over equity transfer contract
ruling_gist_en: Article 147, paragraph 1 of the former Company Law, which provides that 'shares held by the promoters shall not be transferred within three years from the date of incorporation of the company,' is intended to prevent promoters from using the incorporation to seek improper benefits and to evade potential legal liabilities through the transfer of shares.

Wang Hua equity transfer contract dispute
full_text_en:
Zhang Guiping v. Wang Hua — Dispute over Equity Transfer Contract

【Ruling Summary】

I. Article 147(1) of the former Company Law, which provides that "shares held by the promoters of a company shall not be transferred within three years from the date of incorporation of the company," is intended to prevent promoters from using the establishment of a company to seek improper benefits and from evading the legal liabilities they may incur by transferring their shares.

II. Where a promoter of a joint stock limited company enters into an equity transfer agreement with another person within three years after the incorporation of the company, stipulating that the transfer of shares will be registered in the name of the transferee after the expiration of the three-year period, and further agrees in the agreement to entrust the exercise of the rights attaching to the shares to the transferee during such period, such equity transfer contract does not violate Article 147(1) of the former Company Law. The fact that the parties agree, during the statutory lock-up period for promoters' shares, that the transferor will entrust the exercise of the equity rights to the future transferee also does not violate any mandatory legal provisions. Furthermore, prior to the formal registration of the share transfer, such arrangements do not relieve the transferring promoter of their legal liabilities nor of their shareholder responsibilities. Accordingly, the equity transfer contract should be recognized as lawful and valid.

Plaintiff (Counter-defendant): Zhang Guiping, male, 55 years old, Chairman of Suning Universal Group, residing at West Beijing Road, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant (Counter-claimant): Wang Hua, male, 45 years old, Chairman of Jiangsu Jinsheng Group, residing at Zhongshan North Road, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

The plaintiff, Zhang Guiping, filed a lawsuit with the Jiangsu High People's Court against the defendant, Wang Hua, concerning a dispute over an equity transfer contract.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The plaintiff and the defendant, Wang Hua, are both promoters and shareholders of Nanjing Pudong Construction Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Pudong Company"). Pudong Company was established on September 20, 2002. The plaintiff contributed RMB 18 million, holding 18 million shares of Pudong Company, representing 18% of the shares; the defendant contributed RMB 17 million, holding 17 million shares, representing 17% of the shares. After the establishment of Pudong Company, due to project development needs, the company's registered capital was increased from RMB 100 million to RMB 200 million. The plaintiff increased its contribution to RMB 64 million, raising its shareholding ratio to 32%; the defendant increased its contribution to RMB 34 million, maintaining a shareholding ratio of 17%. From June 2004 onwards, the defendant repeatedly contacted the plaintiff on his own initiative, expressing a desire to transfer all of his shares in Pudong Company to the plaintiff. After negotiations, the plaintiff agreed to acquire all of the defendant's shares at a premium price of RMB 83 million, which was 2.44 times the defendant's actual investment. On October 22, 2004, the two parties formally signed a "Share Transfer Agreement," in which the defendant undertook that, until the share transfer procedures were completed, he authorized the plaintiff to exercise all rights and assume all obligations of the defendant as a shareholder. If the plaintiff unilaterally terminated this agreement, he would pay the defendant a special compensation of RMB 415 million; if the defendant breached the agreement, he would also pay the plaintiff a special compensation of RMB 415 million. Since both parties were promoters of Pudong Company, and at the time of signing the "Share Transfer Agreement" the company had been established for less than three years, the parties also signed an "Interim Management Agreement" to ensure a lawful and smooth transfer of shares. After signing the above agreements, the plaintiff strictly performed his obligations as agreed. As of December 31, 2004, the plaintiff had paid a total of RMB 81 million to the defendant. The remaining RMB 2 million, according to the signature of the defendant's agent, was to be settled after the completion of the share transfer procedures. However, on January 8, 2005, the defendant issued a "Notice of Repossession of Shares" to the plaintiff, claiming that the plaintiff's delayed payment and shortfall of RMB 2 million constituted a fundamental breach of contract, and simultaneously revoked all agreements and powers of attorney signed with the plaintiff. The defendant's act of breaching the contract after receiving RMB 81 million was contrary to good faith. The plaintiff requests the court to order the defendant to continue performing the "Share Transfer Agreement" and the "Interim Management Agreement" signed by both parties, and to pay the plaintiff a special compensation of RMB 415 million as stipulated in the "Share Transfer Agreement."

Defendant's Defense: 1. The "Share Transfer Agreement" and the "Interim Management Agreement" signed by the plaintiff, Zhang Guiping, and the defendant violate mandatory legal provisions and the provisions of the "Articles of Association of Nanjing Pudong Construction Development Co., Ltd." (hereinafter "Pudong Company Articles of Association"), and are therefore invalid. The defendant is both a promoter and a director of Pudong Company, and at the time of signing the "Share Transfer Agreement," Pudong Company had been established for less than three years. According to Article 147 of the "Company Law of the People's Republic of China" (hereinafter "Company Law"), shares held by promoters of a joint stock limited company shall not be transferred within three years from the date of incorporation; directors, supervisors, and managers shall declare to the company the shares they hold and shall not transfer them during their term of office. Article 28 of the "Pudong Company Articles of Association" also provides: "Shares held by promoters shall not be transferred within three years from the date of incorporation of the company." Accordingly, at the time the "Share Transfer Agreement" and the "Interim Management Agreement" were signed, the shares held by the defendant could not yet be transferred. The plaintiff, in order to achieve the purpose of formally not transferring the ownership of the disputed equity but actually being able to exercise it immediately, circumvented the law by agreeing in the above agreements that, before the defendant actually transferred the equity, all shareholder rights (including profit rights) and director rights of Pudong Company enjoyed by the defendant would be fully authorized to the plaintiff. Through this, the plaintiff actually enjoyed and exercised the Pudong Company equity owned by the defendant, and the defendant had essentially performed the obligations agreed upon in the agreements. Therefore, the shareholder rights and obligations of the disputed shares have been completely transferred to the plaintiff for enjoyment and assumption. Consequently, the "Share Transfer Agreement" and the "Interim Management Agreement" signed by both parties clearly circumvent the mandatory legal provisions and the provisions of the company's articles of association, and are invalid. 2. Even if the "Share Transfer Agreement" and the "Interim Management Agreement" are valid, Zhang Guiping has no right to demand the defendant pay special compensation for breach of contract. The plaintiff's statements regarding the performance of the agreements are inconsistent with the facts, and the alleged breach of contract by the defendant has no factual basis. The plaintiff claims to have strictly performed his obligations as agreed, but in reality, until the plaintiff filed the lawsuit, the plaintiff still owed the defendant RMB 2 million in equity transfer consideration. The plaintiff's claim that "the defendant's agent signed to acknowledge" does not exist. The facts are as follows: on the morning of December 31, 2004, the defendant dispatched financial personnel to the plaintiff's office to collect the equity transfer payment. However, the plaintiff's personnel deliberately created difficulties for various reasons. It was not until around 9:00 p.m. that day that the plaintiff issued a check for RMB 38 million to the defendant's personnel, while stating that the remaining RMB 2 million would be settled after the completion of the share transfer procedures were confirmed, and required the defendant's relevant personnel to include the above content in the receipt; otherwise, the check would not be delivered. Under these circumstances, the defendant's relevant personnel signed the receipt without the defendant's consent. However, this signature only indicated that the defendant's personnel confirmed receipt of the check for RMB 38 million, and did not mean they acknowledged that the plaintiff could pay RMB 2 million less. There was no situation where "the remaining RMB 2 million is to be settled after the completion of the share transfer procedures are confirmed." According to the "Share Transfer Agreement" signed by both parties, any modification or supplementation of the agreement must be made by a written agreement signed by both parties; personnel dispatched by the defendant had no right to decide unilaterally without the defendant's own authorization. The plaintiff's statements regarding the performance of the agreements are inconsistent with the facts, and the defendant did not breach the contract. On December 31, 2004, the defendant did not personally come to collect the payment for valid reasons, and the "Share Transfer Agreement" signed by both parties did not require that the defendant must personally come to collect the money. Given that the RMB 38 million the plaintiff claimed to have paid actually arrived in the account only on January 4, 2005, and that there was still RMB 2 million unpaid, the defendant's issuance of the "Notice of Repossession of Shares" on January 8, 2005, was a normal reaction to the plaintiff's failure to perform on time and in full, and was a reasonable act, not a breach of contract. After the issuance of the "Notice of Repossession of Shares," it did not actually achieve the effect of repossessing the shares and revoking relevant authorizations. Since the defendant issued the notice, except that the disputed shares have not been transferred due to the statutory prohibition period, the plaintiff has been normally exercising the Pudong Company shareholder rights and director rights authorized to him by the defendant. 3. The "Share Transfer Agreement" and the "Interim Management Agreement" signed by both parties are manifestly unfair. These agreements contain a large number of clauses that unilaterally increase the defendant's burden. For example, in Article 8 of the "Share Transfer Agreement" regarding liability for breach of contract, the plaintiff only pays the special compensation of RMB 415 million in the event of a fundamental breach of contract, i.e., "unilaterally terminating this agreement prematurely," while the defendant is required to pay the special compensation of RMB 415 million in any event of breach of contract, i.e., "violating Article 6 and other relevant clauses."

On June 7, 2005, the defendant, Wang Hua, filed a counterclaim, arguing that the "Share Transfer Agreement" and the "Interim Management Agreement" signed with the plaintiff and counter-defendant, Zhang Guiping, are not only invalid agreements that violate mandatory legal provisions, but are also manifestly unfair agreements concluded by fraudulent means that Wang Hua is entitled to apply to the court to rescind. He requests a ruling that the "Share Transfer Agreement" and the "Interim Management Agreement" signed by both parties be declared invalid and rescinded. The reasons are as follows: In October 2004, Wang Hua and Zhang Guiping negotiated the share transfer. During the negotiation of the share transfer price, Zhang Guiping provided Wang Hua with a financial statement of Pudong Company as of July 1, 2003, and stated that the net asset value of Pudong Company at that time was only RMB 0.98 per share, and the price for this share transfer should be determined with reference to this net asset value. Subsequently, after negotiation, the two parties reached a share transfer agreement on October 22, 2004, at a price of RMB 2.44 per share. In April 2005, due to a dispute arising during the performance of the above share transfer contract, Zhang Guiping filed a lawsuit against Wang Hua. During the process of responding to the lawsuit, Wang Hua learned that after its establishment in September 2002, Pudong Company acquired two plots of land — Pudong Garden and Venice Water City, located in Pukou District, Nanjing — from the Nanjing Municipal Land Department in October 2002, intended for real estate development. In September 2003, Zhang Guiping had arranged for the preparation of Pudong Company's 2003 "Profit Forecast Report" (which was audited by Nanjing Yonghua Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd.). According to this report, the above plots had appreciated by RMB 26.924 million and RMB 704.7 million respectively as of September 2003. Based on this calculation, the net asset value of Wang Hua's shares at the same time could reach RMB 157.6349 million, meaning the value of those shares had already reached RMB 4.64 per share. Moreover, from 2003 to 2004, the real estate market in Nanjing remained extremely active, and land prices rose rapidly. Therefore, by October 2004, the value of Wang Hua's shares in Pudong Company had already far exceeded RMB 4.64 per share. However, in order to defraud Wang Hua of the huge profits from the land appreciation of Pudong Company, Zhang Guiping deceived Wang Hua. During the process of signing the agreement with Wang Hua, he intentionally only presented the financial statements that did not reflect the true value of Pudong Company's shares, and concealed the "Profit Forecast Report" that could reflect the true value of Pudong Company's shares. As a result, Wang Hua transferred his Pudong Company shares, which were actually worth more than RMB 4.64 per share, to Zhang Guiping at only RMB 2.44 per share. Therefore, Zhang Guiping engaged in fraudulent conduct during the process of signing the above agreements, and the agreements thus reached are manifestly unfair and should be rescinded by law.

The plaintiff in this case and counter-defendant, Zhang Guiping, responded to the counterclaim: The counterclaim filed by the defendant in this case and counter-claimant, Wang Hua, has no basis whatsoever, and the court is requested to dismiss the counterclaim. First, Zhang Guiping did not deceive or conceal anything from Wang Hua; the share transfer price was the final result of negotiation between the two parties. At the time of negotiating the transfer price, the parties did not, and could not, use an audit report from more than a year ago as a so-called reference. Moreover, as early as the first interim shareholders' meeting of Pudong Company held on July 1, 2003, the financial audit report had already been distributed to all shareholders of the company. Since Wang Hua did not attend the meeting, the audit report was brought to Wang Hua by other attendees after the meeting. It is absurd for Wang Hua to now use this as a basis for being deceived. Wang Hua was fully aware of the appreciation of the land owned by Pudong Company. Since the establishment of Pudong Company, Wang Hua, as the second-largest shareholder, had participated in the company's formation, land negotiations, capital increases, and other work, and was well aware of the continuous appreciation of the company's land. In January 2004, Wang Hua, together with shareholders Xu Shanglong, Zhu Zaoying, Wu Juanling, and others, sued the Nanjing Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce, seeking to revoke the registration of Pudong Company's capital increase and the changes in the shareholders' capital contributions and shareholdings. By that time, the fact that the land owned by Pudong Company had further increased in value, driven by the Jiangsu Provincial Government's strategy of developing along the Yangtze River, had become common knowledge. It is particularly important to emphasize that this transfer was actively proposed by Wang Hua himself through various channels, and he specifically proposed the price for the share transfer. During the second-instance trial of the administrative litigation against the Nanjing Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce in which Wang Hua participated, Wang Hua repeatedly used mobile phone text messages to express his desire for Zhang Guiping to acquire his shares, using his agreement to withdraw the appeal in that case as leverage, urging Zhang Guiping to consider his request as soon as possible. The specific transfer plan was also proposed by Wang Hua: to adopt the method of multiplying the original share price by four, used by another shareholder of Pudong Company, Zeng Huansha. This resulted in four times Wang Hua's original 17 million shares, plus the later capital increase of RMB 17 million, totaling RMB 85 million. Zhang Guiping agreed to the acquisition, and after negotiations, a transfer agreement was ultimately reached at a price of RMB 83 million. Second, the share transfer agreement reflects the true intention of both parties and is not manifestly unfair. According to relevant legal provisions, a contract may be deemed manifestly unfair if one party, by taking advantage of its superior position or the other party's lack of experience, causes a significant imbalance in the rights and obligations of the parties, violating the principles of fairness and equal exchange. This is the legal standard for determining whether a contract is manifestly unfair. The share transfer agreement involved in this case did not have the above circumstances at the time of its formation. The rights and obligations stipulated in the share transfer agreement were reciprocal, embodying the principles of fairness and equal exchange. Wang Hua's claim that the company's share price had already reached RMB 4.64 per share at that time was merely a forecast, and there is a significant gap between such forecasts and actual equity interests. Zhang Guiping's acceptance of Wang Hua's request for share transfer entailed significant risk and pressure. Therefore, the parties very carefully stipulated a special compensation clause. Third, the relevant agreements for the share transfer did not violate any mandatory legal provisions and are lawful and valid.

Facts Found by the Jiangsu High People's Court:

On September 20, 2002, Pudong Company was legally established with a registered capital of RMB 100 million. The plaintiff in this case and counter-defendant, Zhang Guiping, and the defendant in this case and counter-claimant, Wang Hua, as promoters and shareholders of Pudong Company, contributed RMB 18 million and RMB 17 million respectively, holding 18% and 17% of the shares of Pudong Company. On October 22, 2004, Wang Hua, as Party A, and Zhang Guiping, as Party B, signed a "Share Transfer Agreement," stipulating: Party A confirms that the registered capital of Pudong Company is RMB 200 million, and as of the signing of this agreement, Party A holds 34 million natural person shares of Pudong Company (representing 17% of the total share capital). Party A agrees to transfer the above shares (hereinafter "subject shares") to Party B at a price of RMB 2.44 per share, totaling RMB 83 million. At the same time, Party A must provide Party B with tax invoices for the entire transfer amount. Party B agrees to acquire the above subject shares for RMB 83 million. Both parties agree that Party B shall pay Party B the share transfer price of RMB 83 million in two installments. Within 10 days after this agreement takes effect, Party B shall pay Party A RMB 43 million. Prior to this, the deposit of RMB 20 million paid by Party B to Party A under the "Interim Management Agreement" shall be automatically applied to the share transfer price. Before December 31, 2004, Party B shall pay Party A the remaining share transfer price of RMB 40 million. Articles 4 and 5 of the agreement stipulate: Both parties shall commence the authorization procedures for the share transfer period simultaneously with the signing of this agreement. The period from the signing of this agreement until the subject shares held by Party A are transferred to Party B's name as scheduled is the interim period. The rights and obligations of the parties during the interim period shall be separately stipulated in an "Interim Management Agreement." Article 6 of the agreement stipulates the rights and obligations during the interim period and the share transfer period, confirming that Party A shall issue an irrevocable power of attorney to Party B, authorizing Party B to exercise the duties of a director and shareholder rights of Pudong Company on behalf of Party A, and Party A shall not interfere with or hinder Party B's exercise of shareholder rights over the subject shares. Without Party B's written consent, Party A shall not exercise or entrust any third party to exercise the shareholder rights, director rights, or other rights related to the subject shares; Party A shall not request to change or revoke the "Share Transfer Agreement," and shall not refuse to perform the obligations stipulated in the "Share Transfer Agreement"; Party B has the right to attend Pudong Company's shareholders' meetings as Party A's agent and exercise voting rights and other shareholder rights based on the number of subject shares; Party B enjoys all profit rights and the right to re-transfer enjoyed by Party A as a shareholder of Pudong Company during the interim period, and bears the risks during the interim period, etc. Article 7 of the agreement stipulates: After both parties complete the share registration procedures, Party B shall acquire the subject shares and enjoy the corresponding rights and assume the corresponding obligations as an investor and shareholder of Pudong Company under the subject shares. Article 8 of the agreement stipulates: If Party B unilaterally and prematurely terminates this agreement, Party B shall pay Party A a one-time special compensation of RMB 415 million and shall compensate Party A for the economic losses thereby incurred. If Party A violates Article 6 and other relevant clauses of this agreement, Party A shall also pay Party B a special compensation of RMB 415 million. Party B also has the right to choose to rescind this agreement or demand that Party A continue to perform this agreement. Article 10 of the agreement stipulates: This agreement shall take effect on the date of signature by Party A and Party B in person, and shall terminate on the date when the shares held by Party A are legally and effectively transferred to Party B's name in accordance with the provisions of the Company Law. Both parties agree that if national laws or policies change, modifying the conditions and restrictions on the transfer of shares of promoters of joint stock limited companies, the effective date of this agreement shall be adjusted accordingly in accordance with the new laws and policies. However, matters involving the transfer price of the subject shares, share quantity, and other matters shall not be changed and shall remain as stipulated in this agreement.

On the same day, the defendant in this case and counterclaim plaintiff Wang Hua, as Party A, and the plaintiff in this case and counterclaim defendant Zhang Guiping, as Party B, signed the *Transitional Management Agreement*. Articles 1, 2, and 3 of the agreement set forth the purpose and background for the parties' execution of the transitional agreement and reaffirmed the rights and obligations between them. It provided that during the transitional period, all rights of Party A in the subject shares shall be exercised by Party B, and Party B shall correspondingly assume all liabilities arising therefrom. The agreement also provided that Party B shall pay Party A a deposit of RMB 20 million on the date of signing this agreement, and upon the effectiveness of the *Share Transfer Agreement*, such deposit shall automatically offset the share transfer price. If Party B prematurely terminates this agreement without authorization, Party B shall have no right to demand the return of the deposit from Party A. If Party A violates any provision of Article 3 of this agreement, it shall return twice the deposit to Party B; if returning twice the deposit is still insufficient to compensate for the losses caused to Party B, it shall further pay compensation in the amount specifically agreed upon by the parties. This agreement shall become effective upon Party B's payment of the deposit to Party A.

After the execution of the *Share Transfer Agreement* and the *Transitional Management Agreement*, the defendant in this case and counterclaim plaintiff Wang Hua signed a resignation application addressed to the board of directors of Pudong Company, resigning from his position as a director of the company, and issued a *Power of Attorney* to the plaintiff in this case and counterclaim defendant Zhang Guiping as agreed, fully authorizing Zhang Guiping to exercise on his behalf all rights enjoyed under Wang Hua's shares in Pudong Company. It also confirmed that such authorization would remain valid and irrevocable until Wang Hua transferred all shares under his name to Zhang Guiping. On October 22, 2004, Zhang Guiping paid Wang Hua a deposit of RMB 20 million by check; on October 29 of the same year, he paid Wang Hua a further share transfer price of RMB 23 million by check, receipted by Chen Ying. Within ten days after the agreement was signed, including the deposit of RMB 20 million, Zhang Guiping paid Wang Hua a total of RMB 43 million as the share transfer price, and Wang Hua confirmed receipt. On December 28, 2004, Wang Hua wrote to Zhang Guiping, confirming that the other party should pay an additional RMB 40 million before December 31, 2004, urging him to perform the share transfer agreement on time, and informing the other party: "If the above payment is overdue, I will take back the 34 million shares of individual shares in Pudong Company, and the RMB 43 million already paid will also be treated as liquidated damages for breach of contract and will not be refunded."

On December 30, 2004, the plaintiff in this case and counterclaim defendant Zhang Guiping issued a *Payment Notice* to the defendant in this case and counterclaim plaintiff Wang Hua, requesting Wang Hua to come to his office on the 17th floor of Suning Universal Building on December 31, 2004, to receive the share transfer price of RMB 40 million and to go through the confirmation procedures for the full payment of the share transfer price. On December 31, 2004, employees Zhang Yi and Chen Ying of Jinsheng Real Estate Investment Group Co., Ltd. (where Wang Hua served as legal representative), as handling persons, issued a *Receipt* to Zhang Guiping, stating: "Received on behalf of Zhang Guiping from Suning Company the share transfer price of RMB thirty-eight million (by check). The remaining RMB two million in share transfer price shall be settled after the share transfer procedures are completed and confirmed. Handled by Chen Ying and Zhang Yi on behalf of Wang Hua." The receipt was also stamped with the financial seal of Jinsheng Real Estate Investment Group Co., Ltd.

On January 8, 2005, the defendant in this case and counterclaim plaintiff Wang Hua issued a *Notice of Share Repossession* to the plaintiff in this case and counterclaim defendant Zhang Guiping. The notice stated that Zhang Guiping should have paid the full share transfer price of RMB 40 million by December 31, 2004. However, it was not until January 4, 2005, that Zhang Guiping paid Wang Hua RMB 38 million. Given that Zhang Guiping delayed payment and still owed RMB 2 million, this had constituted a fundamental breach of contract. From that date, the *Share Transfer Agreement* and the *Transitional Management Agreement* signed by the parties on October 22, 2004, were terminated, and simultaneously, all legal documents such as powers of attorney issued by Wang Hua pursuant to Article 6 of the *Share Transfer Agreement* were also invalidated. Wang Hua still held 17% of the shares in Pudong Company and enjoyed all shareholder rights attached to those shares.

On February 25, 2005, the defendant in this case and counterclaim plaintiff Wang Hua declared to the Registration Division of the Nanjing Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce: "From this date onward, any changes concerning my 17% shareholding in Pudong Company, and any capital increase or equity changes in Pudong Company, must be confirmed by my personal presence; otherwise, I will pursue the legal liability of the responsible persons according to law."

The court further finds: On April 16, 2004, the defendant in this case and counterclaim plaintiff Wang Hua sent the same text message to the plaintiff in this case and counterclaim defendant Zhang Guiping from two mobile phones, stating: "Mr. Zhang, regarding the share transfer negotiations yesterday, I think according to Zeng Shuisha's transfer ratio, 17% × 4 = 68 million + 17 million = 85 million yuan. I have invested a long time and played a significant role in the entire capital increase."

On March 11, 2004, *Southern Weekly* published a substantial report on the appreciation of Pudong Company's land and the resulting disputes among some shareholders, which included an interview with the defendant in this case and counterclaim plaintiff Wang Hua himself. The report clearly stated that another cause of the internal disputes among Pudong Company's shareholders was "the rapid surge in the price of Pudong Company's 4,500 mu of land. ... The land price of the 4,500 mu increased nearly threefold, with the potential profit from the land price appreciation alone reaching as high as 1.6 billion yuan, of course not including the even greater profits from building residential houses on the 4,500 mu of land."

The above facts are evidenced by the evidence provided by both parties, and neither party disputes them.

The issues in dispute in this case are: 1. Whether the *Share Transfer Agreement* and the *Transitional Management Agreement* in this case are valid and can be rescinded, i.e., whether the above agreements violate Article 147 of the Company Law and the provisions of the *Articles of Association of Pudong Company*, and whether there were circumstances such as price fraud or obvious unfairness in the signing; 2. If the above agreements are valid, whether the plaintiff in this case and counterclaim defendant Zhang Guiping constituted a fundamental breach of contract in paying the consideration for the subject shares, and whether the defendant in this case and counterclaim plaintiff Wang Hua could terminate the contracts; 3. Whether the liquidated damages agreed upon in the parties' agreement are excessively high, and if so, how they should be adjusted.

The Jiangsu High People's Court holds as follows:

I. On the issue of whether the *Share Transfer Agreement* and the *Transitional Management Agreement* are valid and can be rescinded

(1) As promoters of Pudong Company, the plaintiff in this case and counterclaim defendant Zhang Guiping and the defendant in this case and counterclaim plaintiff Wang Hua, two years after the establishment of Pudong Company, on October 22, 2004, signed the *Share Transfer Agreement* and the *Transitional Management Agreement*, agreeing that after the "transitional period," Wang Hua would transfer the subject shares under his name to Zhang Guiping. The above agreement does not violate the provisions of Article 147 of the Company Law that "Promoters of a company shall not transfer the shares they hold in the company within three years from the date of the company's establishment. Directors, supervisors, and managers of the company shall declare to the company the shares they hold in the company and shall not transfer them during their term of office," nor does it violate the relevant provisions of the *Articles of Association of Pudong Company* or the public interest, and should be deemed lawful and valid.

First, the main duty of promoters of a joint stock limited company is to establish the company. Promoters need to bear responsibility for the consequences of a failed company establishment, and if the company suffers losses during the establishment process due to the promoters' fault, the promoters must also bear corresponding liability. After the company is successfully established, the status of promoter is replaced by that of shareholder, and their rights and obligations toward the company are the same as those of other non-promoter shareholders. Considering that some improper acts of promoters may have delayed legal consequences and liabilities, if a promoter withdraws from the company by transferring shares before the consequences actually occur, it would be difficult to hold them accountable, which is detrimental to protecting the lawful rights and interests of others or the public. Therefore, it is necessary to prohibit promoters from transferring the shares they hold within a certain period. The legislative purpose of Article 147(1) of the Company Law is precisely to prevent promoters from using the company's establishment to seek improper benefits and from evading potential legal liabilities through share transfers. Paragraph 2 of that article, which provides that "Directors, supervisors, and managers of the company shall declare to the company the shares they hold in the company and shall not transfer them during their term of office," is also based on the same legislative purpose.

Second, the act of transferring shares by promoters prohibited by Article 147 of the Company Law refers to the actual transfer of shares by promoters within three years from the date of the company's establishment. The law does not prohibit promoters from entering into contracts in advance for the transfer of shares after the three-year period from the company's establishment. As long as the shares are not actually delivered, there is no change in shareholder status or equity relationship; that is, the promoter who intends to transfer shares remains a shareholder of the company, and their legal liability as a promoter is not exempted by signing an agreement to transfer shares. Therefore, an agreement between a promoter and another person to transfer shares after the three-year period from the company's establishment does not violate the prohibitive provisions of Article 147 of the Company Law and should be deemed lawful and valid. In this case, based on the provisions of Articles 5 and 6 of the *Share Transfer Agreement* signed by the parties regarding the transitional period, Article 7 regarding "procedures for changing share registration," Article 10 regarding "lawfully and effectively transferring the shares held by Party A to the name of Party B in accordance with the provisions of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China" and "if laws and national policies change, modifying the conditions and restrictions on the transfer of shares by promoters of a joint stock limited company, the effective time of the contract shall be adjusted accordingly in accordance with the new laws and policies," it can be determined that both parties were fully aware of the restrictions on the transfer of shares by promoters of the company. Therefore, although the parties signed the share transfer agreement within three years after the company's establishment, they explicitly agreed that the shares would be actually transferred after the expiration of the "transitional period," i.e., three years after the establishment of Pudong Company. At the same time, after signing the *Share Transfer Agreement* and the *Transitional Management Agreement*, the defendant in this case and counterclaim plaintiff Wang Hua signed a resignation application addressed to the board of directors of Pudong Company, resigning from his position as a director of the company, and no longer served as a director. In summary, the above agreement between the parties clearly does not violate the provisions of Article 147 of the Company Law or the relevant provisions of the *Articles of Association of Pudong Company*, and should be deemed a lawful and valid contract.

Third, the plaintiff in this case and counterclaim defendant Zhang Guiping and the defendant in this case and counterclaim plaintiff Wang Hua did not actually transfer the shares within three years after the company's establishment, and there was no violation of Article 147 of the Company Law. In this case, Wang Hua held registered shares. According to Article 145 of the Company Law, which provides that "Registered shares shall be transferred by endorsement of the shareholder or by other methods provided by laws or administrative regulations. The transfer of registered shares shall be recorded by the company in the register of shareholders with the name or title and domicile of the transferee," the determination of whether registered shares have been transferred should be based on the records in the register of shareholders and the industrial and commercial registration. In this case, according to the register of shareholders of Pudong Company and the company's industrial and commercial registration, Wang Hua was still a shareholder and promoter of Pudong Company, and the subject shares in question still belonged to Wang Hua.

Fourth, according to the *Transitional Management Agreement* and the *Power of Attorney* signed by the plaintiff in this case and counterclaim defendant Zhang Guiping and the defendant in this case and counterclaim plaintiff Wang Hua, all rights and obligations of Wang Hua as a shareholder during the transitional period were authorized to Zhang Guiping for exercise. The nature of the *Transitional Management Agreement* is a share or equity custody agreement, and the parties formed a de facto share custody relationship, i.e., Wang Hua remained the shareholder in law and in name, while Wang Hua's rights and obligations as a shareholder of Pudong Company were actually enjoyed and assumed by Zhang Guiping. Since the Company Law of China does not prohibit the custody of company shares or custody relationships, the *Transitional Management Agreement* signed by the parties is lawful and valid. Although the parties agreed in the agreement that all obligations and liabilities of Wang Hua as a shareholder of Pudong Company during the transitional period would be assumed by Zhang Guiping, such an agreement is only internally effective between the parties and has no legally binding effect on third parties. Precisely because the *Transitional Management Agreement* does not exempt Wang Hua from his responsibilities as a promoter and shareholder, the acts of Wang Hua and Zhang Guiping in signing the *Transitional Management Agreement* and the *Power of Attorney* should be confirmed as lawful and valid.

Fifth, the *Share Transfer Agreement* and the *Transitional Management Agreement* do not constitute a situation of concealing illegal purposes under a lawful form. As stated above, the fundamental purpose of the parties in entering into the contracts was to transfer the shares three years after the company's establishment, with the plaintiff in this case and counterclaim defendant Zhang Guiping exercising the equity rights of the defendant in this case and counterclaim plaintiff Wang Hua during the transitional period; this purpose is not illegal. The form and content of the above agreements are all lawful and valid, and they do not violate the provision of Article 28 of the *Articles of Association of Pudong Company* that "Shares held by promoters shall not be transferred within three years from the date of the company's establishment." Wang Hua's counterclaim argument that the execution and performance of the above agreements effectively allowed Zhang Guiping to obtain all rights and interests under Wang Hua's shares in Pudong Company, that Wang Hua no longer bore the risks and obligations as a shareholder, that the parties had substantially transferred the shares, and thus that the agreements violated the prohibitive provisions of the Company Law and the *Articles of Association of Pudong Company* regarding the transfer of shares by promoters of the company and should be deemed invalid, lacks factual and legal basis and is not adopted.

(2) At the time of signing the above agreements, there was no situation of price fraud by the plaintiff in this case and counterclaim defendant Zhang Guiping against the defendant in this case and counterclaim plaintiff Wang Hua, nor was there any obvious unfairness. First, the content of the mobile phone text messages sent by Wang Hua to Zhang Guiping between April 16, 2004, and May 18, 2005, shows that it was Wang Hua who made an offer or counter-offer regarding the share transfer price. Wang Hua requested to refer to the share transfer model of Zeng Shuisha (also known as Zeng Huansha), a former shareholder of Pudong Company, i.e., original shares were to be acquired at four times their value, and capital increase shares were to be returned at cost. At that time, Wang Hua's original shares in Pudong Company were 17 million shares, and his capital increase shares were 17 million shares, totaling 34 million shares. Ultimately, after negotiations, the parties agreed on a share transfer price of RMB 83 million; based on 34 million shares, this price was 2.44 times Wang Hua's original shares. Second, both Wang Hua and Zhang Guiping were entrepreneurs engaged in long-term industrial operations and should have been aware of the actual value of the subject shares and whether the transfer price was reasonable. Wang Hua voluntarily proposed a calculation method for the share transfer price to Zhang Guiping, and in fact, the parties negotiated based on this method, finally determining the subject share transfer price of RMB 83 million. Therefore, there was no price fraud by Zhang Guiping against Wang Hua, nor was there any situation where one party took advantage of its superiority or the other party's inexperience, resulting in rights and obligations that clearly violate fairness and the principle of equal and voluntary compensation, thereby constituting obvious unfairness. Third, Wang Hua argued that when Zhang Guiping signed the above agreement with him on October 22, 2004, he only provided the financial statements of Pudong Company as of July 1, 2003, while concealing the actual situation of the appreciation of Pudong Company's land, thereby acquiring his shares at a low price, which constituted fraud. In fact, Wang Hua, as a director and shareholder of Pudong Company, should have been aware of the company's situation. On March 11, 2004, *Southern Weekly* interviewed Wang Hua; according to the report, Wang Hua was already aware of the appreciation of Pudong Company's land at that time. Wang Hua's counterclaim argument that it was not until Zhang Guiping sued him that he learned from Pudong Company's *2003 Profit Forecast Report* about the significant land appreciation and that the value of his shares in Pudong Company had reached RMB 4.64 per share as of September 2003 is inconsistent with the facts and is not credible. Furthermore, Wang Hua's counterclaim was based on calculation using Pudong Company's *2003 Profit Forecast Report*; since that report was merely a forecast, it cannot be equated with the company's actual property condition or the actual value of the company's equity. Accordingly, Wang Hua's claim that Zhang Guiping committed price fraud, rendering the contract obviously unfair, lacks factual basis and is not supported.

In summary, when the parties signed the *Share Transfer Agreement* and the *Transitional Management Agreement* in this case, there was no price fraud or obvious unfairness; the above agreements are both the true expressions of the parties' intentions and are not contracts that can be rescinded according to law.

II. On the issue of whether the plaintiff in this case and counterclaim defendant Zhang Guiping constituted a breach of contract in paying the consideration for the subject shares, and whether the defendant in this case and counterclaim plaintiff Wang Hua could terminate the contracts

(1) The payment of RMB 38 million by the plaintiff in this case and counterclaim defendant Zhang Guiping to the defendant in this case and counterclaim plaintiff Wang Hua as part of the share transfer price did not constitute delayed performance. The *Share Transfer Agreement* signed by the parties only required Zhang Guiping to pay the remaining share transfer price of RMB 40 million to Wang Hua before December 31, 2004; the method of payment was not specified. Therefore, as long as Zhang Guiping completed the payment within the performance period, he would not be in breach. In this case, Zhang Guiping paid Wang Hua RMB 38 million by check before December 31, 2004, and Wang Hua acknowledged receipt of the said amount. The fact that the funds were credited to the account after December 31, 2004, should not be used as a basis for finding Zhang Guiping in delayed performance. Accordingly, it should be determined that Zhang Guiping's payment of the said amount complied with the parties' contractual agreement and did not constitute delayed performance.

(2) The expression made by Chen Ying and Zhang Yi, financial personnel of Jinsheng Real Estate Investment Group Co., Ltd., as agents of Wang Hua (the defendant and counterclaim plaintiff), regarding the RMB 2,000,000 yet to be paid by Zhang Guiping (the plaintiff and counterclaim defendant), to the effect that "the remaining RMB 2,000,000 share transfer price shall be settled after the share transfer procedures are completed and confirmed," shall be deemed as a new agreement between the parties on the payment of part of the consideration. Zhang Guiping's retention of the RMB 2,000,000 pending settlement after completion and confirmation of the share transfer procedures does not constitute a breach of contract. First, on December 30, 2004, Zhang Guiping issued a "Payment Notice" to Wang Hua, notifying Wang Hua to come the next day to collect the RMB 40,000,000 and to go through the formalities for confirming receipt of the full share transfer price. Since the parties explicitly agreed in the "Share Transfer Agreement" that Wang Hua would transfer his shares in Pudong Company to Zhang Guiping at a price of RMB 83,000,000, and that Wang Hua must provide Zhang Guiping with tax invoices for the full transfer price, Zhang Guiping's requirements in the above "Payment Notice" fully complied with the agreement and the purpose of the transaction, as well as with normal transaction practices. Wang Hua's claim that there was no need to go through the formalities for confirming the completion of the share transfer payment on December 31, 2004, is unfounded and is not accepted. Second, on December 31, 2004, Wang Hua himself did not go to Zhang Guiping's office but instead sent Chen Ying and Zhang Yi, financial personnel of Jinsheng Real Estate Investment Group Co., Ltd., carrying the company's financial seal, to handle the procedures for collecting the payment. Wang Hua did not entrust Chen Ying and Zhang Yi to bring a receipt signed by him personally confirming receipt of the full RMB 83,000,000 transfer price, nor did he issue a written power of attorney authorizing Chen Ying and Zhang Yi to go through the formalities for confirming receipt of the full RMB 83,000,000 transfer price. As a result, Zhang Guiping and Wang Hua were unable to complete the formalities for confirming the delivery of the full share transfer price. Therefore, when Chen Ying and Zhang Yi, on behalf of Wang Hua, confirmed that "the remaining RMB 2,000,000 share transfer price shall be settled after the share transfer procedures are completed and confirmed," and affixed the financial seal of Jinsheng Real Estate Investment Group Co., Ltd., this act should be regarded as Wang Hua having reached a new agreement with Zhang Guiping on the payment of the remaining RMB 2,000,000 share transfer price. Third, Wang Hua claimed that he only instructed Chen Ying and Zhang Yi to go to Zhang Guiping's office to collect the payment, without giving any other authorization, and that Chen Ying and Zhang Yi therefore exceeded their authority of agency, and he refused to recognize the above commitment made by Chen Ying and Zhang Yi regarding the payment of the remaining RMB 2,000,000 share transfer price. The court held that since Chen Ying and Zhang Yi were subordinate employees of Jinsheng Real Estate Investment Group Co., Ltd., of which Wang Hua was the legal representative, and the two were sent by Wang Hua to Zhang Guiping's office to collect the payment, it would be contrary to common sense if, without Wang Hua's authorization, Chen Ying and Zhang Yi exceeded their authority of agency in making the commitment that "the remaining RMB 2,000,000 share transfer price shall be settled after the share transfer procedures are completed and confirmed." Furthermore, Wang Hua failed to provide evidence to prove that he had imposed restrictive authorization on the agency actions of Chen Ying and Zhang Yi and had informed Zhang Guiping of such restrictive authorization. Therefore, the commitment made by Chen Ying and Zhang Yi on behalf of Wang Hua that "the remaining RMB 2,000,000 share transfer price shall be settled after the share transfer procedures are completed and confirmed" shall be regarded as Wang Hua's true intention. Fourth, Wang Hua also claimed that the commitment made by Chen Ying and Zhang Yi regarding the remaining RMB 2,000,000 share transfer price was made under duress from Zhang Guiping and was not the true intention of Chen Ying, Zhang Yi, or Wang Hua himself. However, Wang Hua failed to provide corresponding evidence to prove this, and therefore this claim is not recognized. In summary, Zhang Guiping's payment of the RMB 38,000,000 share transfer price does not constitute a delay in performance, and his failure to pay the remaining RMB 2,000,000 share transfer price to Wang Hua was also recognized by Wang Hua. Therefore, Zhang Guiping's payment of the subject share transfer price does not constitute a breach of contract. Wang Hua's exercise of the right to terminate the contract on the ground that Zhang Guiping's payment constituted a breach of contract has no factual or legal basis. Wang Hua's actions constitute a breach of contract, and he shall bear corresponding liability for breach of contract. At the same time, there is no impossibility of performance in law or fact in this case, and Zhang Guiping's claim for continued performance of the agreement between the parties should be upheld. Given that during the trial of this case, Pudong Company has been established for more than three years, Wang Hua shall, in accordance with the contract between the parties, go through the relevant procedures for the share transfer with Zhang Guiping.

3. Whether the liquidated damages agreed upon in the agreement between the parties are excessively high, and if so, how they should be adjusted

In this case, where the defendant and counterclaim plaintiff, Wang Hua, breached the contract, the plaintiff and counterclaim defendant, Zhang Guiping, while requesting Wang Hua to continue performance of the contract, may also request Wang Hua to bear liability for breach of contract by paying liquidated damages or compensating for losses. However, the agreement in the contract between the parties to pay special compensation of five times the transfer amount, i.e., RMB 415,000,000, is clearly excessively higher than the losses caused to Zhang Guiping by Wang Hua's breach of contract. Pursuant to the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 114 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which states that "if the agreed liquidated damages are excessively higher than the losses caused, a party may request the people's court or an arbitration institution to make an appropriate reduction," such liquidated damages should be appropriately reduced. In this case, Zhang Guiping shall bear the corresponding burden of proof as to the losses caused to him by Wang Hua's breach of contract. Since Zhang Guiping is unable to further adduce evidence of other losses beyond the interest losses on working capital loans caused by Wang Hua's breach of contract, and his request that Wang Hua pay him special compensation of five times the share transfer amount, i.e., RMB 415,000,000, is disputed by Wang Hua, Zhang Guiping's claim is not upheld. For Wang Hua's liability for breach of contract, the interest on working capital loans during the period when the RMB 81,000,000 was occupied by Wang Hua should be used as a reference basis for appropriate adjustment. It is determined that Wang Hua shall pay Zhang Guiping liquidated damages of RMB 5,000,000.

In summary, the "Share Transfer Agreement" and the "Transition Period Management Agreement" signed between the plaintiff and counterclaim defendant, Zhang Guiping, and the defendant and counterclaim plaintiff, Wang Hua, represent the true intentions of both parties and their contents are lawful and valid. Zhang Guiping's request for continued performance of the agreement shall be upheld. Zhang Guiping did not breach the contract during the performance of the agreement. Wang Hua's claim that Zhang Guiping's failure to pay the RMB 38,000,000 on time and his outstanding balance of RMB 2,000,000 constituted a fundamental breach of contract, and his request for termination of the contract, have no factual or legal basis. His unilateral termination of the agreement has constituted a breach of contract, and he shall bear corresponding liability for breach of contract and pay Zhang Guiping liquidated damages of RMB 5,000,000. Accordingly, the Jiangsu High People's Court rendered the following judgment on December 6, 2005: (1) The "Share Transfer Agreement" and the "Transition Period Management Agreement" signed between the plaintiff and counterclaim defendant, Zhang Guiping, and the defendant and counterclaim plaintiff, Wang Hua, are valid; (2) Wang Hua shall, within 10 days after this judgment takes effect, go through the relevant procedures for the share transfer with Zhang Guiping in accordance with the contract; (3) After the above share transfer procedures are completed, Zhang Guiping shall immediately pay Wang Hua the share transfer price of RMB 2,000,000; (4) Wang Hua shall, within 10 days after this judgment takes effect, pay Zhang Guiping liquidated damages of RMB 5,000,000; (5) Zhang Guiping's other claims are dismissed; (6) Wang Hua's counterclaim is dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 2,085,010 is to be borne by Zhang Guiping in the amount of RMB 1,563,757.50 and by Wang Hua in the amount of RMB 521,252.50; the litigation preservation fee of RMB 666,145 is to be borne by Wang Hua; the counterclaim acceptance fee of RMB 425,010 and the court express mail fee of RMB 200, totaling RMB 425,210, are to be borne by Wang Hua.

After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, neither party appealed, and the judgment of first instance has taken legal effect.

Note: The Company Law in force prior to the revision was applied at the time of trial in this case. Article 142 of the revised Company Law shortened the period restricting promoters from transferring shares to one year.
